messages:
marta_customer: Hey team — hitting intermittent 429s from our on-prem/customer-managed gateway during nightly batch window (03:20 UTC). p99 latency spikes and some auth failures. Trace ids in logs: trace=0xabc123,0xabc124. Any quick ideas?

sara_support: Thanks Marta — can you paste a short log snippet and say which ingress/gateway you're running (Envoy/nginx/HAProxy) + how many gateway pods? Also approximate RPS during the burst.

marta_customer: We're on Envoy-based gateway (customer image from last private release). 6 gateway pods behind k8s node pool. Bursts come from a batch job that opens ~600 concurrent connections for ~40–90s, RPS peeks ~1200. Logs: 
```
[03:20:12] gateway-1 envoy [warning] 429 rate_limiter - client_id=acct-123 x-client-id=acct-123 path=/v1/generate status=429 remaining=0
[03:20:13] gateway-3 envoy [info] rate_limit=throttled token_bucket_used=100 capacity=100 refill=10/s
```
Also headers we see on clients: x-rate-limit-limit:100, x-rate-limit-remaining:0

raj_eng_sre: Sounds like per-instance token bucket exhaustion + burst coalescing across pods. When lots of parallel clients start at same time you get synchronized refill windows -> short high-rate bursts that exceed leaky-bucket capacity. Two paths: 1) server-side smoothing (increase bucket size or refill rate, distributed rate limiter) 2) client-side splay/jitter to spread load.

raj_eng_sre: Example Envoy local rate-limit (token-bucket) tweak — increase fill and burst capacity or switch to distributed redis-backed ratelimit service:
```yaml
# Envoy local rate limit filter (example)
- name: envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.local_ratelimit.v3.LocalRateLimit
    stat_prefix: http_local_rate_limiter
    token_bucket:
      max_tokens: 500       # increase burst capacity
      tokens_per_fill: 50   # refill amount
      fill_interval: 1s     # refill interval
```

raj_eng_sre: If you use an external rate-limit service (lyft/ratelimit) you can keep small per-pod local buckets and a global quota in Redis, which avoids per-pod bursts.

devx_bob: Also recommend adding jitter on the job ramp-up — splay the batch start across job instances or add randomized sleep between connections. If the job is k8s CronJob you can use an init step to randomize offset: 
```bash
# in job container
sleep $((RANDOM % 30))s
```
This often removes the synchronized spike. :mechanical_arm:

raj_eng_sre: For nginx-ingress users a quick mitigation via annotations: 
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rate-after: "1m"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "50"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "200"
```
But since you're Envoy-based, tune the envoy token_bucket or switch to global ratelimit service.

raj_eng_sre: If you want to change per-customer scope, route by header (X-Client-ID) and configure the rate limiter key to be that header. That prevents noisy neighbors sharing a single bucket.

sara_support: Temporary mitigation options: 1) bump local max_tokens (fast but increases momentary TTFB for everyone), 2) enable distributed ratelimit backed by Redis (safer), 3) advise customer to add client jitter (low risk). We can also add a temporary canary config to two pods to validate.

marta_customer: Can you paste the minimal EnvoyFilter manifest I should apply for testing (we can do a canary on 2 pods)?

raj_eng_sre: Minimal patch (EnvoyFilter-like pseudo manifest) — adapt to your control plane: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: local-rate-limit-patch
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      app: customer-gateway
  configPatches:
    - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
      match:
        context: SIDECAR_INBOUND
      patch:
        operation: INSERT_BEFORE
        value:
          name: envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit
          typed_config:
            "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.local_ratelimit.v3.LocalRateLimit
            stat_prefix: test_local_rl
            token_bucket:
              max_tokens: 300
              tokens_per_fill: 30
              fill_interval: 1s
```
Apply to two pods first, monitor x-rate-limit-* headers and envoy stats: `envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_pending_overflow` and our internal `local_rate_limiter.*`.

raj_eng_sre: Quick repro command you can run from k8s job/pod to recreate the spike: 
```bash
# runs 600 concurrent short connections
hey -n 5000 -c 600 -z 1m http://<gateway-ip>/v1/generate
# or ApacheBench
ab -n 2000 -c 200 http://<gateway-ip>/v1/generate
```
Watch for 429s and then tail logs: `kubectl logs -l app=customer-gateway -c envoy --tail=200`

ratebot: [alert] rate-limit-service: elevated throttle events detected for svc=customer-gateway (5m window).

marta_customer: Great — we'll canary the EnvoyFilter on 2 pods and add jitter to the job. I'll post results in ~30m. Thanks all! :pray:

sara_support: Thanks — ping us if 429s persist after canary & client splay, we'll escalate to infra for Redis-backed ratelimit rollout.
